review_notes: I read the whole target file, plus the definitions in Model.lean (`deck`, `basis`, `laplacian`, `spatialPartial`, `divergence`) and the neighbouring SheetFlows files (Differential, DirectForce, Clocks, PlanarHamiltonian). I grepped the SheetFlows and MathematicalPhysics trees for existing `@[simp]` lemmas and for uses of `simp [deck]`, `simp [basis]` and the `laplacian` sum expansion. The only attribute-level simp issues I found are the two reported below. I did not report `divergence_sub`, `divergence_smul` or `divergence_sum`: they carry smoothness hypotheses, so making them simp lemmas would need side-condition discharge and I saw no concrete benefit. I cannot run Lean, so I have not checked that the proposed lemmas compile or that adding them as simp lemmas causes no clashes. In particular, I am not sure `deck_apply` would fire cleanly after `Pi.add_apply` in the existing proofs, and I did not look for a canonical-form clash elsewhere (e.g. with `Pi.single_apply`).

findings.excerpt:
have hL : laplacian u = ∑ j, spatialPartial (spatialPartial u j) j := by
    funext t x
    simp [laplacian]
findings.problem: `laplacian` is a bare `def` with a pointwise body, and the file needs its field-level expansion as a sum of iterated partials. That rewrite is not a named lemma. It is proved twice as an identical local `have hL`, with the same `funext t x; simp [laplacian]` proof, once in `laplacian_divergence_free` and once in `laplacian_mean_zero`. Anyone who needs `divergence_sum` or `meanZero_sum` on a Laplacian must rediscover and re-prove this equation. The only simp lemma about `laplacian` in this part of the library is `laplacian_zero`, so there is no canonical form to rewrite into.
findings.proposed_change: Add a named lemma next to the `laplacian` definition or in DirectForce.lean. It should state `laplacian u = ∑ j, spatialPartial (spatialPartial u j) j` for a general `u : Field`, with proof `funext t x; simp [laplacian]`. Optionally add a pointwise version `laplacian u t x = ∑ j, ...`. Both occurrences of `hL` then become `rw [laplacian_eq_sum]`. I would deliberately not mark it `@[simp]`: it would unfold `laplacian` everywhere and compete with `laplacian_zero`. Keep it as an explicit rewrite lemma, or as a `simp only` argument.
findings.benefit: This removes duplicated proof text and fixes one canonical expansion of `laplacian`. Later lemmas that reduce a Laplacian to a finite sum (divergence, mean-zero, smoothness, periodicity) can reuse it instead of re-proving it. It also avoids the `simp [laplacian]` unfold-everything pattern.

evidence.excerpt:
def laplacian (u : Field) : Field :=
  fun t x => ∑ j : Fin 3, spatialPartial (spatialPartial u j) j t x
have hL : laplacian u = ∑ j, spatialPartial (spatialPartial u j) j := by

findings.declaration: periodic_integral_divergence_zero / face_front_eq_back_deck / wrapSpace_add_deck (unfolding `deck` and `basis` by hand)
findings.problem: The simp interface for `deck` and `basis` has no coordinate lemma. `deck` and `basis` are plain `def`s (`deck k = fun j => 10 * (k j : ℝ)` and `basis j = Pi.single j 1`), and there is no `deck_apply` or `basis_apply` for the SheetFlows versions. The file therefore unfolds the definitions: `simp [deck]` twice in `face_front_eq_back_deck`, `simp only [Pi.add_apply, wrapSpace, deck, Int.fract]` in `wrapSpace_add_deck`, and `simp only [basis] at *` in `periodic_integral_divergence_zero`. The last of these unfolds `basis` in every hypothesis and in the goal, which is a blunt, non-local rewrite. The same unfolding recurs across SheetFlows (e.g. `simp [basis]` in ShearCore.lean and Localization.lean, `simp only [Pi.add_apply, deck, ...]` in Clocks.lean). A different, unrelated `basis_apply` simp lemma exists for the planar `basis` in PlanarHamiltonian.lean, which shows the intended pattern.
findings.proposed_change: In Model.lean, right after the definitions, add `@[simp] theorem deck_apply (k : Fin 3 → ℤ) (j : Fin 3) : deck k j = 10 * (k j : ℝ) := rfl`. Add `@[simp] theorem basis_apply (j i : Fin 3) : basis j i = if i = j then 1 else 0` (proved by `simp [basis, Pi.single_apply]`), or alternatively `basis_self` and `basis_of_ne`. Proofs can then use `simp` without unfolding the definitions. `simp only [basis] at *` becomes unnecessary or can be replaced by a targeted rewrite. Both `deck_apply` and `basis_apply` are terminating, orientation-safe coordinate evaluations. I recommend them only because of the many repeated unfoldings, not because the identity looks simple.
findings.benefit: The definitions `deck` and `basis` are only ever used through their coordinates, so one canonical coordinate rewrite replaces many ad hoc `simp [deck]` and `simp [basis]` calls. Proofs stay robust if the definition bodies change. It also removes the global `simp only [basis] at *`.

evidence.excerpt: def deck (k : Fin 3 → ℤ) : Space := fun j => 10 * (k j : ℝ)
def basis (j : Fin 3) : Space := Pi.single j 1
simpa only [Pi.add_apply, deck, mul_comm (10 : ℝ)] using (hg j).int_mul (k j) (x j)
@[simp] theorem basis_apply (i j : Fin 2) : basis i j = if j = i then 1 else 0 := by
